H. Tribe is a professor of constitutional law at Harvard University.
President Trump has already declared his intention to pardon himself. He said he could "under [the] current interpretation" of the Constitution, which is true. But there is no such interpretation. There is only the Constitution, and the Constitution is explicit. original: For professors, publishing in elite journals is an unavoidable part of university life. The grueling process of subjecting work to the up-or-down judgment of credentialed scholarly peers has been a cornerstone of academic culture since at least the mid-20
sampled:
th century, and today it is a major source of prestige and income. But elite journals aren’t always the most appropriate choice for academic papers: a growing body of evidence suggests that a more diverse range of journals (and, as a result, more diverse content) may be better for the individual scholar and for the advancement of academic knowledge.

Over the past decade, scholars have begun to analyze the distribution of journal articles across publication venues. USC announced Thursday it would appeal NCAA sanctions it considers "excessive." And even before those plans became official, Trojans football coaches were calling recruits and getting out the message that the penalties could be reduced.
"They're trying to appeal
sampled:
to see if they can reduce it," said USC quarterback Max Browne, who won't be a junior this season and is expected to be a top-five pick in the NFL draft. "I would do the same thing if I was a coach. If you think you have a chance to get it reduced, you're going to try."
USC's appeal is in response to the NCAA's findings that it committed 30 major rules violations between 2004 and 2010. The most severe penalties include a one-year bowl ban, scholarship reductions, and scholarship limits in football.

Trojans football coach Lane Kiffin was the first to reach out to Browne about the news, and he said he hopes the appeal will work.

"I said, 'Hey, I heard we might get our scholarships back,' " Kiffin said. "And he said, 'Oh, that would be awesome.' "

Franklin police arrested a gunman Friday morning after he sequestered himself inside a home and refused to come out.
Police said Martin Zaragoza, 22, was on the run after he fired several shots outside a home on Granville Road during a
sampled:
domestic dispute with his ex-girlfriend.
Police said Zaragoza fired three or four shots from an assault rifle during the shooting and barricaded himself in the home.
No one was injured during the shooting, but Zaragoza refused to come out of the home Friday morning, police said.
Neighbors were told to stay inside while police negotiated with Zaragoza.
After several hours, Zaragoza came out of the home with his hands up, police said.
Zaragoza was arrested on charges of aggravated assault, aggravated menacing, and unlawful possession of a weapon.
